core_obligations: Note that a PID is a Noetherian Bezout ring, and use the splitting lemma to reduce to the case where M is torsion (proof lines 37896-37898).
Since M is finite and torsion, its annihilator is nonzero; say fM = 0 with f nonzero, so that M may be viewed as a module over R/fR (proof lines 37898-37900).
Use that R/fR is Noetherian of dimension zero — a step the author states is a small detail omitted — to write R/fR = prod R_j as a finite product of Artinian local rings (proof lines 37901-37904).
Observe that each R_j, being a local ring and a quotient of a PID, is a generalized valuation ring in the sense of the earlier lemma, again with a small detail omitted (proof lines 37905-37907).

Write M = prod M_j with M_j = e_j M for the idempotents e_j corresponding to the factors, and apply the structure lemma for modules over a generalized valuation ring to get M_j = bigoplus_{i=1..n_j} R_j/\overline{f}_{ji}R_j (proof lines 37908-37911).
Choose lifts f_{ji} in R and elements g_{ji} with (g_{ji}) = (f_j, f_{ji}) for a lift f_j of the uniformizer, and conclude M = bigoplus R/g_{ji}R as an R-module (proof lines 37912-37918).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that every finite module M over a principal ideal domain R is isomorphic to R^{oplus r} oplus bigoplus_{i=1..n} R/f_iR for some r, n >= 0 and nonzero f_i in R (source lines 37886-37894). The proof is a multi-stage reduction. Since a PID is a Noetherian Bezout ring, the splitting lemma applied there reduces the problem to the case where M is torsion; being finite, M then has nonzero annihilator, say fM = 0, so M may be viewed as a module over R/fR (proof lines 37896-37900). The substantive part is the structure of R/fR: since it is Noetherian of dimension zero — a fact the author states is a small detail omitted — it is a finite product of Artinian local rings R_j by the dimension-zero proposition, and each R_j, being a local quotient of a PID, is a generalized valuation ring in the sense of the earlier lemma, again with a small detail omitted (proof lines 37901-37907). Writing M = prod M_j with M_j = e_j M for the idempotents e_j corresponding to the factors, the structure lemma for modules over a generalized valuation ring gives M_j = bigoplus_{i=1..n_j} R_j/\overline{f}_{ji} R_j (proof lines 37908-37911). The final step lifts the quotients back to R: choosing lifts f_{ji} in R and elements g_{ji} with (g_{ji}) = (f_j, f_{ji}) where f_j is a lift of the uniformizer, the proof concludes M = bigoplus R/g_{ji}R as an R-module (proof lines 37912-37918). The non-routine content is the decomposition of R/fR into Artinian local factors and the lifting of the resulting cyclic quotients back to elements of R.
